view.stem: 下面哪些比较能正确说明力的大小、方向或作用点会影响作用效果？选择所有正确的描述。

options.text: 固定同一弹簧的一端，在弹性范围内沿同一方向拉它；静止时，较大的拉力使弹簧伸得更长。这是在比较力的大小。
在可忽略水平阻力的平地上，同一辆静止小车在同一点受到大小相等的水平推力：一次向东，一次向西；它开始运动的方向不同。这是在比较力的方向。
对同一扇门施加大小相等、垂直门面且同向的推力；推把手处比推靠近铰链处更容易使门转动。这是在比较力的作用点。
在同一扇门的把手处施加大小相等、方向相反的垂直推力；由于大小和作用点相同，它们使门转动的方向也相同。

intent.task: Judge controlled causal comparisons that collectively preserve force magnitude, direction and application-point dependence rather than just recalling three attribute names.
intent.source_solution: Independent pre-option solution: the same elastic spring under a larger same-direction static pull extends farther; reversing an otherwise comparable action can reverse motion or door turning; equal perpendicular pushes farther from a door hinge have greater turning effect. Magnitude, direction and application point must not be silently substituted for one another. The door comparison is conditional on equal perpendicular forces and a common axis.
intent.unit_reason: One native multiple unit evaluates complete examples across all three attributes. Three distinct valid comparisons and a direction-insensitive false comparison retain the source's collective causal task without separate attribute-label clicks.
limitations: Complete examples and the controlled comparisons are supplied; autonomous invention, apparatus selection and unaided explanation of examples are not tested.
The spring, cart and hinged-door cases sample the three dependencies; they do not establish a universal quantitative response law for every body.
The direction examples partially overlap conceptually, but the cart tests translation and the false door claim tests turning; neither establishes a marked result elsewhere.

rationales.derivation: Same spring, direction and elastic static conditions isolate magnitude; a larger pull produces greater extension in this range.
From rest under the stated east versus west pushes, the direction of the induced motion changes while magnitude and application point are held comparable.
Equal perpendicular forces have turning effect proportional to lever arm about the same hinge; the handle is farther away, so changing application point changes turning effect.
Opposite perpendicular forces at the same door point create opposite turning senses, not the same sense.
rationales.misconception: Discard direction from the force description, retaining only equal magnitude and equal point; infer identical action and therefore the same turning direction for the two opposite pushes.

view.stem: 两个力的大小都是 $12\,\mathrm{N}$，一个向东，一个向西。哪种解释正确说明了为什么力是矢量？

options.text: 两力大小相同而方向不同，表示它们需要同时给出大小和方向，因此它们是不同的力矢量。
两力的数值和单位相同，因而是同一个力矢量；向东或向西不改变对力的完整描述。
力只要具有作用点就是矢量；大小和方向都可以不指定，作用点已经给出了完整的力矢量。
力是矢量，因为有力时物体就一定在运动；物体的运动速度就是这个力的大小和方向。

intent.task: Apply the magnitude-and-direction vector definition and distinguish equal magnitudes from equal force vectors.
intent.source_solution: Force has both magnitude and direction. Equal 12 N magnitudes with opposite directions give distinct vectors. Application point matters for a body's response but does not replace vector components. Motion or its velocity is not the force itself.
intent.unit_reason: The source asks for one causal definition-level explanation, so one single unit compares complete reasons rather than separate true/false term tests.
limitations: Recognition of a complete reason does not test unaided explanation or wording of the definition.
The supplied equal-magnitude opposite-direction case samples the definition; vector addition, resultant forces and general equality proofs are not tested.

rationales.derivation: A vector's magnitude and direction are both required. East and west differ in direction despite equal 12 N magnitudes, so the vectors differ.
Equal numerical magnitudes and units do not equate opposite-direction vectors.
rationales.misconception: Replace each force by its positive scalar magnitude 12 N; compare only those scalar records and infer that the two complete vectors are the same.

rationales.derivation: Location alone does not specify a vector's magnitude and direction, and an application point cannot supply missing values.
rationales.misconception: Promote the application's location, one of the factors affecting a body's response, to the entire definition of a vector; delete magnitude and direction as supposedly unnecessary.

rationales.derivation: A force can act on a stationary supported body, and force is not velocity. Motion does not define vector status.
rationales.misconception: Identify force with visible motion, then identify its components with the object's velocity; conclude that force is a vector because velocity has size and direction.

view.stem: 用有箭头的线段表示作用在物体上的力。结合图中的 $A$ 和箭头，哪种完整说明正确？

options.text: $A$ 是线段始端和力的作用点，箭头表示右上方向；线段长度按选定比例表示力的大小，但这幅图没有给出可换算牛顿数的比例。
$A$ 是线段始端和力的作用点，力的方向从右上箭头尖端指回 $A$；线段长度按选定比例表示力的大小。
$A$ 是线段始端和力的作用点，箭头表示右上方向；画同样粗的线段就表示同样大的力，线段长度不承担大小信息。
$A$ 是线段始端和力的作用点，箭头表示右上方向；不必给出牛顿与长度的比例，量出这幅图的线段长度就能算出力的牛顿数。

intent.task: Interpret the full force-diagram correspondence: start/application, arrow direction and calibrated length, including the absence of a numerical calibration in this actual figure.
intent.source_solution: Use an arrowed segment beginning at the receiving body's application point. Its head gives force direction and its complete length gives magnitude under a declared scale L=F/S. Fig-68 begins at A and points up/right; its source supplies no numerical force scale, so numerical force cannot be inferred.
intent.unit_reason: One complete-description single unit keeps the three representation roles together. It is not three isolated labels or an uncalibrated pixel-length question.
limitations: The visible origin and direction support interpretation; recognizing the correct rule does not prove constructing an arrow, placing its application point, choosing a scale or measuring length unaided.
Fig-68 is qualitative and uncalibrated; no magnitude, measured angle or physical centimetre length is inferred from the screen.

figure_observations.observation: Opened the actual approved durable SVG as a complete 640 px rendering. One body occupies the lower-left; A is the body/shaft origin and the single arrow points up/right. Entire far-right head and bottom body are visible; no scale, force number or extra vector is present.

rationales.derivation: The body/shaft point A is the start, the head points up/right, and magnitude requires the chosen force-per-length ratio. No ratio is given for this qualitative figure.
A directed force runs from start to head, so the stated head-to-A direction reverses the depicted force.
rationales.misconception: Read a directed segment backwards, treating its arrowhead as the place to begin following the shaft; retain the true A location and scale rule but assign the opposite direction.

rationales.derivation: Under a fixed scale magnitude is encoded by length, not stroke thickness. Equal thickness does not imply equal force.
rationales.misconception: Use visual boldness as the magnitude channel; regard a uniformly thick shaft as a complete magnitude specification and discard proportional length.

rationales.derivation: A measured drawing length alone lacks a conversion to newtons. The same uncalibrated segment can represent many force magnitudes under different scales.
rationales.misconception: Assume an undeclared one-newton-per-length-unit calibration, measure the drawing and automatically turn its length number into a force number without specifying the unit ratio.

view.stem: 图中左右是同一个静止面粉袋的两种受力表示。按照本课对重力和重量的区分，哪种解释正确？

options.text: $F$ 是作用在袋上的向下重力，所以始端在袋内；$P$ 是袋作用在支承物上的向下重量，所以始端在袋与支承物的接触处。
$F$ 是袋作用在支承物上的向下重量，所以始端在袋内；$P$ 是作用在袋上的向下重力，所以始端在袋与支承物的接触处。
$F$ 是作用在袋上的向下重力，所以始端在袋内；$P$ 是支承物作用在袋上的向下支持力，所以始端在袋与支承物的接触处。
$F$ 和 $P$ 都是作用在袋上的向下力；因为两力大小相等，袋内点和支承物接触点可以互换，不影响它们的受力对象。

intent.task: Explain why gravity and weight diagrams have different receiving bodies and application origins in the supported-body convention.
intent.source_solution: Gravity acts on the bag, represented from an interior resultant point. Weight is the bag's action on its support and starts at bag/support contact. Both point down in this stationary supported case; the upward support-on-bag reaction is not P. Equal magnitudes do not make recipients or application points interchangeable.
intent.unit_reason: A complete-recipient explanation is one single unit. It uses the approved teaching image but requires force-on-object meaning, not merely matching F/P letters or counting ticks.
limitations: The supported-bag diagram already supplies origin and direction cues; the remaining task is interpreting their different receiving bodies.
Recognition of this supported example does not prove drawing new gravity/weight vectors or transferring the distinction to every suspended configuration.
No precise centre of mass, distributed contact-force law or general equality of weight and gravity in accelerating situations is claimed.
This repeats the application-point principle in later numerical drawing plans; no option is marked correct and later plans still require independent scale and unit judgments.

figure_observations.observation: Opened the actual approved durable SVG as a complete 640 px rendering. F starts inside the left sack and points down through its base; P starts at the right base/support contact and points down below it. Both complete sacks, four current ticks per arrow, both heads, F/P and bottom-left 10 N scale, including the lowest/rightmost P content, are visible.

rationales.derivation: The stated origins match forces on the bag versus on its support. Their common downward directions in this supported static case do not erase the recipient distinction.
B interchanges gravity and weight recipients while retaining the pictured locations, so the meaning of each force is wrong.
rationales.misconception: Memorize two downward arrows but interchange the names gravity and weight; assign support action to the interior F and body gravity to contact P.

rationales.derivation: The support's force on the bag is upward, while P here is the bag's downward action on the support. Both actor/recipient and direction of C's proposed support force are wrong.
rationales.misconception: Treat any force at contact as support-on-body force, then copy the pictured downward arrow without reversing it when exchanging actor and recipient.

rationales.derivation: Equal magnitudes do not make different recipients equal or permit moving a force origin from a body to a different support.
rationales.misconception: Identify forces only by magnitude; collapse gravity and weight into one bag force, then treat all candidate origins as interchangeable because the numerical magnitudes match.

view.stem: 一物体静止在水平支承物上，它的重量为 $400\,\mathrm{N}$；另一次击球时，球在接触点受到向右的水平力 $50\,\mathrm{N}$。下面各方案自行选定比例。哪些方案能正确表示这两个力？选择所有正确方案。

options.text: 两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $100\,\mathrm{N}$：重量画 $4\,\mathrm{cm}$，从物体与支承物的接触处向下；击球力画 $0.5\,\mathrm{cm}$，从球的接触点向右。
重量图用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $200\,\mathrm{N}$，画 $2\,\mathrm{cm}$，从支承接触处向下；击球图用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $10\,\mathrm{N}$，画 $5\,\mathrm{cm}$，从球的接触点向右。
两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $100\,\mathrm{N}$：重量画 $4\,\mathrm{cm}$，从物体与支承物的接触处向上；击球力画 $0.5\,\mathrm{cm}$，从球的接触点向右。
两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $100\,\mathrm{N}$：重量画 $0.25\,\mathrm{cm}$，从支承接触处向下；击球力画 $2\,\mathrm{cm}$，从球的接触点向右。

intent.task: Judge whole two-force drawing plans, retaining each chosen scale, proportional length, receiving-object origin and direction, including valid different scales.
intent.source_solution: The original permits positive self-chosen scales. With common 100 N/cm, lengths are 400/100=4 cm and 50/100=0.5 cm. With separate 200 N/cm and 10 N/cm they are 2 and 5 cm. Weight on horizontal support starts at support contact and points down; the strike starts on the ball's receiving contact and follows the specified horizontal direction. Original horizontal sense and support geometry are unspecified; this view explicitly adds a rightward strike and horizontal resting support.
intent.unit_reason: One native multiple unit evaluates each complete paired plan and retains the relationship between independent scale choices and both force representations. It does not split the source into isolated length clicks or force a unique self-chosen scale.
limitations: Candidates supply the scale choices and spatial descriptions. Autonomous choice of suitable scales, physical ruler construction, point placement and production of both diagrams are not tested.
No new candidate image is authorized; these are complete verbal drawing plans, not recognition of actual newly constructed diagrams or proof of drawing ability.
Horizontal resting support and rightward strike are explicitly authored conditions narrowing the unspecified source geometry and horizontal sense.
The correct separate-scale plan means the larger physical force can have the shorter drawn arrow; bare lengths across different scales cannot be compared.

rationales.derivation: At 100 N/cm, the full lengths are 4 and 0.5 cm; weight starts on support contact down, and the ball receives a rightward contact force.
Both separately declared positive scales are valid: 400/200=2 cm and 50/10=5 cm. Different scales allow reversed visual length ordering without changing physical force magnitudes.
Lengths are correct, but the body's weight on support is downward. An upward contact arrow would not represent that weight.
rationales.misconception: Replace the body's weight on the support with the support's upward reaction on the body; keep the correct 400 N magnitude and scale but reverse the weight arrow.

rationales.derivation: Under 100 N/cm the lengths must be 4 and 0.5, not 0.25 and 2. D uses inverse ratios.
rationales.misconception: Calculate scale divided by force instead of force divided by scale, then label the results as centimetres: 100/400=0.25 and 100/50=2.

view.stem: K-700 型拖拉机向右牵引工具，此时在牵引连接处对工具施加的水平力达到 $60000\,\mathrm{N}$。用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $10\,\mathrm{kN}$，哪种方案正确表示这个作用在工具上的力？

options.text: 线段长 $6\,\mathrm{cm}$，始端在工具的牵引连接处，箭头向右。
线段长 $60\,\mathrm{cm}$，始端在工具的牵引连接处，箭头向右。
线段长 $\frac{1}{6}\,\mathrm{cm}$，始端在工具的牵引连接处，箭头向右。
线段长 $6\,\mathrm{cm}$，始端在拖拉机的牵引连接处，箭头向左。

intent.task: Determine a complete scaled traction plan with compatible N/kN units, full length, receiving-object origin and force direction.
intent.source_solution: 60000 N=60 kN, so at 10 kN/cm the full length is 6 cm. The depicted force begins on the tool at its traction coupling and points right in the expressly added setup. The original says the traction can reach this magnitude, not that it always does; this view selects that reached-magnitude case and visibly supplies direction and recipient absent from the written source.
intent.unit_reason: One single unit compares full plans for one specified force. The drawing task is not reduced to accepting an isolated 6 cm value: one alternative has that value but reverses actor/recipient and direction.
limitations: The source's direction and contact recipient are not specified; rightward tractor-on-tool traction at the coupling is an explicit added concrete setup.
Recognizing a verbal plan does not prove using a ruler, placing the origin and arrowhead or drawing the six-centimetre segment.
Only the case reaching 60000 N is tested, not every possible operating traction or a constant-maximum claim.
No tractor image, model-history question or new diagram is introduced.

rationales.derivation: Convert 60000 N to 60 kN, divide by 10 kN/cm to obtain 6 cm, and represent the rightward force received by the tool at its coupling.
The scale is 10 kN/cm=10000 N/cm, so the length is 6 cm, not 60. Using 1000 N/cm loses the scale's factor of 10.
rationales.misconception: Recall 1 kN=1000 N but substitute that conversion alone for the complete 10 kN in the scale; use 1000 N/cm instead of 10 times 1000 N/cm, and compute 60000/1000=60 cm.

rationales.derivation: 10/60=1/6 inverts the required force-per-scale quotient; the length is 60/10=6 cm.
rationales.misconception: After correctly converting to 60 kN, reverse the quotient and compute scale magnitude 10 divided by force magnitude 60, then call the result a length.

rationales.derivation: D describes the opposite tool-on-tractor force rather than the requested tractor-on-tool force. The right length alone does not fix the wrong recipient and direction.
rationales.misconception: Exchange the interacting actor and recipient, move the origin from the tool to the tractor, and reverse the direction while retaining the common force magnitude and scale.

view.stem: 一箱砖质量为 $3$ 吨，静止放在水平板车上。取 $g=9.8\,\mathrm{N/kg}$。以下各方案中的重力和重量分别画在两幅图中，每幅都标明自己的比例。哪些方案正确？选择所有正确方案。

options.text: 两力均为 $29.4\,\mathrm{kN}$；两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $10\,\mathrm{kN}$，各画 $2.94\,\mathrm{cm}$。重力从箱内向下，重量从箱与板车接触处作用在板车上向下。
两力均为 $29.4\,\mathrm{kN}$；两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $5\,\mathrm{kN}$，各画 $5.88\,\mathrm{cm}$。重力从箱内向下，重量从箱与板车接触处作用在板车上向下。
两力均为 $29.4\,\mathrm{N}$；两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $10\,\mathrm{N}$，各画 $2.94\,\mathrm{cm}$。重力从箱内向下，重量从箱与板车接触处作用在板车上向下。
两力均为 $29.4\,\mathrm{kN}$；两图均用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $10\,\mathrm{kN}$，各画 $2.94\,\mathrm{cm}$。重力从箱内向下，重量从箱与板车接触处作用在板车上向上。
两力均为 $29.4\,\mathrm{kN}$；重力图用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $10\,\mathrm{kN}$，画 $2.94\,\mathrm{cm}$；重量图用 $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ 表示 $5\,\mathrm{kN}$，画 $5.88\,\mathrm{cm}$。重力从箱内向下，重量从接触处作用在板车上向下。

intent.task: Judge complete gravity-and-weight plans preserving tonne/kg conversion, g-dependent magnitude, independent or common scale choices, both full lengths, different recipient origins and downward directions.
intent.source_solution: The general unsupplemented source gives 3 tonnes=3000 kg and F=P=3000g N in the static supported case. The visible authored g=9.8 N/kg gives 29400 N=29.4 kN. At 10 kN/cm each length is 2.94 cm, at 5 kN/cm each is 5.88 cm. Separate declared scales also validly give 2.94 and 5.88 cm for equal magnitudes. Gravity acts on the crate down from an interior resultant point; weight acts on the cart down at contact.
intent.unit_reason: One native multiple unit retains the complete two-force construction plan and the legitimate nonuniqueness of self-chosen scales. Different valid common and separate scales are independently judged rather than treated as competing unique numerical answers.
limitations: The selected seed contains no numerical g; 9.8 N/kg is an explicit new visible condition, not copied from a solved example or silently imposed on the general source solution.
Candidates supply scales and verbal spatial plans. Autonomous scale design, ruler drawing, point placement, labeling and independent explanation are not demonstrated.
No new candidate diagram is authorized; recognizing these complete plans is not recognizing or producing actual crate drawings.
Horizontal support and stationary conditions settle the downward weight and its equality in magnitude with gravity; no accelerating-cart or suspension generalization is tested.
Different declared scales legitimately permit unequal drawn lengths for equal force magnitudes. No unique self-chosen scale or universal equal-length claim is imposed.

rationales.derivation: 3000 kg times 9.8 N/kg is 29400 N=29.4 kN. At 10 kN/cm both lengths are 2.94 cm, with gravity on crate interior and weight on cart contact, both down.
The same 29.4 kN magnitudes at another legitimate common scale 5 kN/cm require lengths 29.4/5=5.88 cm; recipients and directions remain correct.
The selected g multiplies 3000 kg, not 3 kg. C's scale-to-length arithmetic is coherent for 29.4 N, but that force magnitude is wrong by a factor of 1000.
rationales.misconception: Treat the 3-tonne mass as 3 kg, calculate 3 times 9.8=29.4 N, and then consistently use 10 N/cm to obtain 2.94 cm.

rationales.derivation: The crate acts downward on the cart. Its weight cannot be the upward support reaction, even when magnitude and length are correct.
rationales.misconception: Confuse the cart's upward action on the crate with the crate's weight on the cart; copy that opposite direction into the correctly calculated contact vector without changing the stated recipient.

rationales.derivation: Each figure independently declares its scale. 29.4/10=2.94 and 29.4/5=5.88 cm both encode the same force magnitude; different drawn lengths are valid, and origins/directions preserve the two recipients.

omitted_tasks: Autonomous invention of examples, selection of controlled conditions and unaided explanatory production.
coverage.reason: The complete comparisons retain magnitude, direction and application-point causal distinctions collectively; recognizing supplied examples is meaningful partial coverage, not proof of producing them.

omitted_tasks: Unaided formulation of the reason that force is a vector and transfer beyond the supplied opposite-direction case.
coverage.reason: A whole-reason judgment applies the vector definition instead of asking for its vocabulary alone.

omitted_tasks: Independently constructing, positioning, measuring and labeling a force arrow and independently selecting its scale.
coverage.reason: The complete rule preserves origin, direction and calibrated length while honestly restricting evidence to interpretation of an approved uncalibrated image.

omitted_tasks: Making new gravity/weight drawings and transferring the source distinction to suspended configurations.
coverage.reason: The approved supported-bag teaching image retains the different recipients and application locations. Its existing visual cues are disclosed, not credited as unaided drawing production.

omitted_tasks: Unaided suitable-scale selection, ruler construction and actual production of both force diagrams.
Original unspecified support/suspension arrangement and horizontal left/right sense beyond the explicit authored supported/rightward setup.
coverage.reason: Each alternative is a whole paired scale/length/origin/direction plan, including multiple legitimate scale choices. Correct local lengths alone are insufficient and drawing ability is not claimed.

omitted_tasks: Actual ruler construction and spatial production of the scaled traction arrow.
Autonomous choice of an illustration direction and recipient/contact setup absent from the original.
coverage.reason: The view explicitly selects maximum traction and a concrete rightward tractor-on-tool setup. Its complete-plan judgment preserves N/kN conversion, length, direction and receiving-point meaning.

omitted_tasks: Unaided scale selection and actual ruler/spatial production of both diagrams.
The unsupplemented g-dependent family of magnitudes beyond the explicit visible g=9.8 N/kg numerical instance.
coverage.reason: Full common/separate-scale plans retain 3 tonnes to kg conversion, both magnitudes, scale relations and gravity/weight recipients. The source's broader symbolic solution and production losses remain explicit rather than silently normalized.
